builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
summary: The method replaces Huginn's fixed or broadly uniform recurrence-depth prior with a learned, entropy-regularized prior, and replaces standard input injection with orthogonal injection that removes the state's component along the input. It costs training recurrent-depth models from scratch at 100M–1.6B scale, adds training complexity (learned prior, entropy term, truncated backpropagation), and accepts small accuracy losses from terminal KV sharing and the distilled student. It can fail because fixed-depth training breaks KV sharing, the claimed gains are validated only at small scale, and no pretrained looped checkpoints of production-relevant size are available to adopt directly.
rationale: The gains require pretraining looped models from scratch, which exceeds the reader's budget, but the fixed-point KV-sharing and truncated-backprop results are worth tracking as the architecture family matures.
technique: Looped models with learned depth prior and orthogonal injection

claims.statement: The method replaces Huginn's fixed or broadly uniform recurrence-depth prior with a learned, entropy-regularized prior, and replaces standard input injection with orthogonal injection that removes the state's component along the input. It costs training recurrent-depth models from scratch at 100M–1.6B scale, adds training complexity (learned prior, entropy term, truncated backpropagation), and accepts small accuracy losses from terminal KV sharing and the distilled student. It can fail because fixed-depth training breaks KV sharing, the claimed gains are validated only at small scale, and no pretrained looped checkpoints of production-relevant size are available to adopt directly.

At 1.6B parameters, the learned depth prior with a 3x smaller KV cache matches the downstream-task average of fixed-depth training with the full cache; additionally, a distilled student prefills up to 1.79x faster and RL gradient updates from saved rollout states run 2x faster.
